nodes.name: Chemical bath deposition and annealing
nodes.procedure: Initially, a solution containing nickel sulfate hexahydrate (NiSO₄⋅6H₂O), and iron sulfate heptahydrate (FeSO₄⋅7H₂O) was prepared, with varying molar ratios of nickel to iron depending on target composition (pure Ni for NiO, Ni:Fe = 85:15 for Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O, Ni:Fe = 65:35 for Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O, pure Fe for Fe₂O₃). Potassium persulfate (K₂S₂O₈) was used as the oxidizing agent, and ammonium hydroxide solution (3.5 wt%, 30–33 wt% NH₃ in H₂O) was added as the precipitating agent. The mixture was heated for 20 min at 50 °C, maintaining a consistent temperature using a bain-marie setup. The precipitate was collected via centrifugation and thoroughly washed with distilled water and ethanol. The resulting product was then dried at room temperature for at least 24 h and subsequently annealed at 350 °C for 60 min.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO displays flower-like microsphere morphology which is porous and has high surface area. Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O shows similar but denser and more aggregated flower-like nanosheet morphology with increased active sites. Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O exhibits granular compact morphology. Fe₂O₃ shows needle-like or rod-like morphology characteristic of α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the synthesized catalysts, as shown in Fig. 1b via SEM, reveals distinct structural features. NiO displays a 'flower-like microsphere' morphology, which is porous and has a high surface area... Fe₂O₃ exhibits a needle-like or rod-like morphology, characteristic of α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite)

nodes.characterization_summary: NiO: distinct diffraction peaks matching cubic NiO (JCPDS 47-1049) at 37.32° (111), 43.36° (200), 62.99° (220), 75.56° (311), 79.57° (222). Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O and Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O: nickel ferrite NiFe₂O₄ phase (JCPDS 44-1485) with broad peaks at 35.68° (311), 43.37° (400), 57.37° (511), 63.01° (440). Fe₂O₃: both α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite, JCPDS 33-0664) and dominant γ-Fe₂O₃ (maghemite, JCPDS 39-1356) phases.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of NiO shows distinct diffraction peaks matching the standard pattern for NiO (JCPDS No. 47–1049)... The XRD spectrum of the Fe₂O₃ catalyst reveals the presence of both α-Fe₂O₃ (hematite) and γ-Fe₂O₃ (maghemite) phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: All catalysts show high transparency in visible spectrum (400-800 nm) and strong UV absorption (200-400 nm), retaining optical stability after 24 h in 1 M KOH and surrogate seawater.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further evaluate the materials' optical stability, UV–Vis transmittance spectra were recorded over a 200–800 nm wavelength range under three different solution conditions, as shown in Fig. 2c.

nodes.characterization_summary: Survey spectra show O dominant, Ni in NiO and mixed oxides, Fe in Fe₂O₃ and mixed oxides. High-resolution Ni 2p and Fe 2p confirm NiO species (Ni²⁺) and Fe₂O₃ (Fe³⁺). Increasing FWHM from pure oxides to mixed oxides (Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O, Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O) indicates complex oxidized environment consistent with NiFe₂O₄-like phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental composition of the four catalysts was analyzed using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), as shown in Figure S3... The detailed XPS spectra of the Ni 2p and Fe 2p core-level regions indicate the presence of oxidized chemical environments (Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O Cdl values: ~1.6 mF cm⁻² (1 M KOH), 1.2 mF cm⁻² (1 M KOH + 0.5 wt% NaCl), 0.85 mF cm⁻² (1 M KOH + 2.45 wt% NaCl) before stability test; after test: 1.17 mF cm⁻² and 1.12 mF cm⁻² respectively, confirming high stable ECSA under saline conditions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In 1 M KOH, the electrocatalyst exhibited a high Cdl of ~1.6 mF cm⁻²... Under saline conditions (0.5 and 2.45 wt% NaCl), Cdl values remained substantial (1.2 and 0.85 mF cm⁻², respectively), and slightly increased after the stability test to 1.17 and 1.12 mF cm⁻².

nodes.characterization_summary: After 24 h in surrogate seawater (1 M KOH + 2.45 wt% NaCl): NiO retains flower-like morphology (highest stability), Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O and Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O show minor changes, Fe₂O₃ exhibits significant deterioration with fragmented features.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images (Figure S2) reveal that NiO exhibited the highest structural stability, retaining its initial flower-like microsphere morphology. Ni₀.₈₅Fe₀.₁₅O and Ni₀.₆₅Fe₀.₃₅O showed only minor morphological changes, whereas Fe₂O₃ exhibited significant structural deterioration.
